pedestrian_crossing_intention_qa.Question: Will the pedestrian located at [343, 818, 367, 913] in frame 1 cross the road? Justify your answer with spatial, temporal, mathematical, ego-vehicle, and scene-context reasoning. Conclude the pedestrian’s motives.
pedestrian_crossing_intention_qa.Spatial_Reason: The pedestrian remains consistently positioned on the sidewalk throughout all frames, with their body oriented perpendicular to the road rather than aligned toward a crossing direction, and shows no lateral movement toward the road edge.
pedestrian_crossing_intention_qa.Temporal_Reason: The pedestrian maintains a stationary standing position across all 15 frames with only minimal positional shifts, showing no preparatory movements, forward lean, or head turns toward traffic that would indicate crossing intent.
pedestrian_crossing_intention_qa.Mathematical_Reason: The pedestrian's bounding box shows only small lateral displacement (from x-coordinate 343 to 200) over 15 frames, indicating minimal movement parallel to the road rather than perpendicular crossing motion, with no measurable velocity toward the road.
pedestrian_crossing_intention_qa.Ego_Vehicle_Reason: The ego-vehicle maintains steady speed around 23 mph with minimal deceleration, and the pedestrian shows no responsive movement or positioning changes that would suggest awareness of or interaction with the approaching vehicle.
pedestrian_crossing_intention_qa.Scene_Context_Reason: The urban main road environment lacks crosswalk markings or traffic signals, other group members are also stationary and not crossing, and the pedestrian's attention appears directed away from the roadway rather than toward traffic assessment.
pedestrian_crossing_intention_qa.Conclusion: The pedestrian will not cross because they remain stationary on the sidewalk, face away from the road, show no crossing preparation behaviors, and are part of a group that is also not moving toward the roadway.
